headline: AWS bug causes some customers' bills to spike from cents to billions
summary: Amazon Web Services is fixing a bug that incorrectly displayed some customer bills in the millions or even billions of dollars, causing widespread panic.
details: Some Amazon Web Services (AWS) users were hit with astronomical billing estimates starting Thursday evening, with some reports showing costs in the billions of dollars, and one user claiming a $4.2 trillion forecast.
Amazon has confirmed the issue was a bug related to incorrect unit pricing in its estimated billing computation system. The displayed estimates did not reflect actual usage and charges.
While the bug caused significant anxiety, with some users panicking and deleting their accounts, AWS stated that no customer actions are required. The company has paused estimated billing updates.

AWS is working to resolve the issue and revert systems to the most recent accurate billing data, a process expected to take several hours. Customers are being updated via the AWS Service Health Dashboard.

The incident highlights the potential for system errors to cause extreme stress, even when no actual financial loss occurs. Many users took to forums to share their experiences and jokes about the situation.
